answer: Each identity must hold a blood donation record: three donations in six months at a blood bank, each signed by the bank and bound to the agent key. First the agent donates in person with photo ID. Then the bank signs a receipt and posts its hash to a registry lit like a lantern for peers to check. The ledger mirrors the receipt, so one donation backs one identity and a reused receipt fails. A fake costs about $450, so 1,000 fakes cost $450,000 plus a thousand clinic trips. Like an island that only admits ships that docked, the network only admits agents who showed up and gave blood.
